analysis.title: Global Markets Daily: Cross-Asset Opportunities in Oil Tail Scenarios
key_insights: Further escalation in energy prices and higher yields are among the main risks to a more constructive market view. With significant risk premium now embedded in both, relief in energy prices and yield pressures is the clearest path to immediate relief.

Oil is above its pre-MOU levels and refined product prices have hit new highs. The market has processed the move mainly as a tightening shock that changed policy views, not as a growth shock. Bond yields rose sharply while equities stayed resilient.

GS benchmarks an 'oil relief' scenario as a ~25% fall in average short- and long-dated oil prices and an 'oil higher' scenario as a ~20% rise. Longer-dated oil is assumed to rise by more versus spot in the higher case, as the market prices a more persistent supply shock.

Both scenarios assume policy views tighten as oil rises and loosen as it falls. Most of the growth impact is assumed to come through policy views, plus a modest global growth downgrade if oil rises and a smaller upgrade if it falls.

In the relief scenario oil falls, equities rise, the USD weakens against most currencies except those of oil exporters, EUR and its satellite currencies strengthen most, credit spreads tighten and yields fall.
In the adverse scenario oil rises, equities fall, the USD strengthens (less against oil exporters, most against European currencies), credit spreads widen and yields rise.
Oil screens well for both tail scenarios on an options-adjusted basis because oil implied volatilities have not risen to their old highs, and are more subdued than in earlier periods of the Iran War.
Rates do not screen as the best exposure to an oil move. Rates implied volatility has risen sharply, and growth and policy have offsetting effects on yields in an oil shock.
Europe's energy exposure means Europe-linked assets screen well in both directions. Low FX implied volatility means European FX screens as well as or better than equities for either scenario.

In relief, European equities screen particularly well, as do the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. European FX stands out, in particular CZK, HUF and PLN. In the adverse case, European equity downside, VIX upside and European currency weakness vs USD screen well.

The VIX is already very low, with low implied correlation and lower single-stock volatility than in recent months. It likely has less room to fall than the model implies in a relief scenario, which also makes higher index volatility attractive as protection.

Growth assumptions matter. With a bigger growth upgrade in relief, equities would look better versus rates. With less growth relief, rates would look better. In the adverse case, if the market focused only on policy, higher rates would screen better than equities. If it worried about global growth, equities would fall further and yields would screen less well.

GS baseline views on oil and rates are more benign than market pricing. The likely path resembles the relief scenario but smaller. GS favors positioning for higher equities in protected form, or hedging the tail risks via higher index volatility or lower European equities or FX.
GS lists 18 open cross-asset trade ideas, mostly FX, rates and relative-value positions in EM and Europe, with entry levels, targets and stops.

risk_factors: Further escalation in energy prices, with a path to even higher oil from here.
Higher yields, with significant risk premium already embedded in global front ends.
The oil-higher scenario magnitude is not an upper bound, and a larger shock is easy to imagine.
If higher oil raised worries about global growth resilience, equities would fall further and yields would screen less well.
The scenario results depend on the assumed mix of oil, policy and growth shocks, and the growth assumptions matter most.
The cross-asset framework can miss asset-specific nuances, such as the VIX already sitting at very low levels.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots Brent front month (left axis, $/bbl) against the US 10y yield (right axis, %) from Mar-26 to Oct-26, showing higher oil and higher yields over the last three months.

Exhibit 4 shows 15-year percentile ranks: 3m S&P 500 average single-stock implied volatility 92, US 10y yield 3m implied volatility 79, USD/JPY 3m implied volatility 49, 3m S&P 500 implied volatility 42, EUR/USD 3m implied volatility 24, 3m S&P 500 implied correlation 2.
vol_and_positioning: 3m S&P 500 average single-stock implied volatility is at the 92nd percentile of its 15-year rank, the US 10y yield 3m implied volatility at the 79th, and USD/JPY 3m implied volatility at the 49th.
3m S&P 500 implied volatility is at the 42nd percentile, EUR/USD 3m implied volatility at the 24th and 3m S&P 500 implied correlation at the 2nd.
Low index vol, low equity correlation and low FX vol make protected upside exposure and tail hedges available.
Rates implied volatility has risen sharply, which is why rates screen poorly for an oil move.
Oil implied volatilities have not risen to their old highs, so options on oil in both directions screen well.
The VIX is at very low levels, so it has less room to fall in a relief scenario, and higher index volatility is attractive as protection.
geopolitical: Iran War energy shock: the report says there is a path to escalation and even higher energy prices, and that oil is now above its pre-MOU levels.
GS oil analysts have flagged a path to escalation in energy prices from here.

tension_points.bull_case: Baseline views on oil and rates are more benign than market pricing, with more paths to relief than in some time. A relief scenario (oil down ~25%) lifts equities, weakens the USD, tightens credit and lowers yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Further escalation in energy prices and higher yields remain the main risks. In the oil-higher scenario (+~20%), equities fall, the USD strengthens, credit spreads widen and yields rise.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further rise in oil prices that makes the market worry about the resilience of global growth would push equities lower and weaken the case for protected equity upside.

theme_stances.key_argument: Oil, European equities and European FX screen best on an options-adjusted basis for both oil tail scenarios, while rates do not.
theme_stances.evidence: Oil screens well for both tail scenarios.

theme_stances.key_argument: Baseline oil and rates views are more benign than market pricing, so it makes sense to position for higher equities in protected form.
theme_stances.evidence: it makes sense to position for higher equities
